{{nihongo|'''Kumano Shrine'''|熊野神社 (高島市)}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Ōmi Province]].

Although named Kumano Shrine, there is also a tradition that it is unrelated to the so-called {{ill|Kumano Three Shrines|Q10403700|qid=Q10403700}}.

Formerly, three major routes ran north-south through Takashima District: the Hokurikudō (Nishi-Ōmi road), Akatsuki (Meigetsu) road, and Saba road. Of these, the Meigetsu road ran across Kumano-yama (today's Aibano upland). It is said Oda Nobunaga used this road during his campaign against the Asakura.

Local priestly-family documents (e.g., ''Furumiya Family Documents,'' ''Aiba Family Documents'') record that "the shikinaisha Kumano Shrine originally stood at Nos e in Kumano-yama along Meigetsu road; on March 16, Genki 3, it was burned by Mori Hanbei Tame-mura, and residents moved the sacred symbol into the precinct of {{ill|Hanifu Shrine|ja|波爾布神社|qid=Q11555577}}." The old site name Mikoshi-daira remains, but it is now within a Self-Defense Force training area and inaccessible.

At the former south end (Koga village) and north end (Nishino village) of Meigetsu road were remote worship sites of Kumano Shrine; these correspond to the present Kumano Shrines at Kamikoga in Azumigawa-chō and at Oi in Imazu-chō.

== Enshrined deity ==
* {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kumano Kusubi-no-Mikoto}}

== History ==
It is said to have been moved into Harifu Shrine's precinct by residents of Kumano-yama in the Tenshō era. Until early Meiji, a Kumano festival was held on June 6 with Noh performances.

== Festival ==
* Annual festival: April 20

* {{ill|Izanami|lt=Izanami-no-Mikoto|qid=Q682306}}

== History ==
Shrine tradition says it was rebuilt in Kōnin 14. In old times it was called '''Hakusan-gū''', but in Meiji it changed to the present name. In Meiji 9 it was ranked village shrine.

== Festival ==
* Annual festival: May 1

== Enshrined deity ==
* {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kumano Kusubi-no-Mikoto}}

== History ==
It formerly stood in Nishino village and was moved to the current location in the Eishō era.

It is currently outside animal-damage-prevention fencing, so ordinary worship is generally not possible.

== Festival ==
* Annual festival: April 29
